sources.entry: Meme Search - AI-powered meme search engine. Automatically extracts descriptions from images using vision-language models, then indexes with vector embeddings for semantic and keyword search. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted meme search engine that uses vision-language models to generate descriptions for your images and searches them by keyword or semantic vector similarity.
summary.what_it_does: Meme Search scans meme image directories and generates text descriptions with a local image-to-text model (Florence-2, SmolVLM, or Moondream2 variants) or an OpenAI-compatible vision API. Descriptions are stored in Postgres with pgvector, so you can run keyword search or vector (embedding) search, filter by tags and directory paths, and edit descriptions by hand. The web app supports bulk description generation, directory rescans, and drag-and-drop or paste uploads (JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF; first frame used for GIF descriptions). A read-only, token-authenticated Search API v1 and a dependency-free Python CLI are included, along with an experimental Chromium popup. Deployment is via Docker Compose, with the web UI bound to 127.0.0.1 by default.
use_cases: search my meme collection by what's in the image
auto-describe memes with a vision-language model
semantic search over a local photo or image library
upload and index memes through a web interface
query meme index from a terminal or script
how_to_run: Open the web app on port 3000 (default, bound to 127.0.0.1)
Upload images by drag-and-drop or paste, or mount a meme directory into the meme_search service
notable: Runs image-to-text description generation fully locally by default, with an optional OpenAI-compatible vision API mode where only descriptions are sent externally
Choice of several vision-language models, including an INT8-quantized Moondream2 for lower-memory machines
Read-only Search API v1 with scoped bearer tokens, plus a Python CLI and experimental Chromium popup
Keyword and vector search with tags, directory-path filters, and manual description editing
caveats: The web UI has no user authentication and is supported only on loopback; public or LAN exposure is unsupported
API tokens protect only the /api/v1 endpoints, not the web UI or settings
Docker images are built manually before releases, and multi-platform builds are resource intensive
First description generation is slow while model weights download
